meaning: An organ that produces gametes and reproductive hormones.
example: Testes and ovaries are gonads.
whatItDoes: Testes and ovaries are gonads.
feature: Testes and ovaries are gonads.
importantDistinction: A gonad is an organ, not the gamete it produces.
confusion: A gonad is an organ, not the gamete it produces.

meaning: A reproductive cell containing one chromosome set.
example: A human sperm or egg carries 23 chromosomes.
whatItDoes: A human sperm or egg carries 23 chromosomes.
feature: A human sperm or egg carries 23 chromosomes.
importantDistinction: A gamete is a cell; a reproductive hormone is a chemical signal.
confusion: A gamete is a cell; a reproductive hormone is a chemical signal.

meaning: A reproductive organ or structure.
example: Examples include the testes, ovaries, penis, uterus and vagina.
whatItDoes: Examples include the testes, ovaries, penis, uterus and vagina.
feature: Examples include the testes, ovaries, penis, uterus and vagina.
importantDistinction: A primary organ can continue developing at puberty.
confusion: A primary organ can continue developing at puberty.

meaning: A physical feature associated with sexual maturation that is not a reproductive organ itself.
example: A deeper voice or facial-hair growth can develop at puberty.
whatItDoes: A deeper voice or facial-hair growth can develop at puberty.
feature: A deeper voice or facial-hair growth can develop at puberty.
importantDistinction: Timing alone does not determine whether a characteristic is primary or secondary.
confusion: Timing alone does not determine whether a characteristic is primary or secondary.

meaning: The developmental period when reproductive hormone activity and reproductive capacity increase.
example: Reproductive organs mature and secondary sex characteristics become more noticeable.
whatItDoes: Reproductive organs mature and secondary sex characteristics become more noticeable.
feature: Reproductive organs mature and secondary sex characteristics become more noticeable.
importantDistinction: Puberty does not change a primary organ into a secondary characteristic.
confusion: Puberty does not change a primary organ into a secondary characteristic.

meaning: A chromosome involved in the typical XX or XY pattern of human sexual development.
example: The X and Y are the human sex chromosomes.
whatItDoes: The X and Y are the human sex chromosomes.
feature: The X and Y are the human sex chromosomes.
importantDistinction: Chromosome pattern, hormones and tissue responses are distinct parts of development.
confusion: Chromosome pattern, hormones and tissue responses are distinct parts of development.

meaning: A gene, usually on the Y chromosome, involved in initiating testis development.
example: Its activity helps initiate a developmental pathway.
whatItDoes: Its activity helps initiate a developmental pathway.
feature: Its activity helps initiate a developmental pathway.
importantDistinction: SRY is a gene, not testosterone or a whole chromosome.
confusion: SRY is a gene, not testosterone or a whole chromosome.

meaning: A male gonad containing seminiferous tubules and testosterone-producing interstitial cells.
example: It contributes sperm and hormones to reproduction.
whatItDoes: It contributes sperm and hormones to reproduction.
feature: It contributes sperm and hormones to reproduction.
importantDistinction: The testis is the organ; the scrotum is the pouch supporting it.
confusion: The testis is the organ; the scrotum is the pouch supporting it.

meaning: The pouch containing the testes outside the main body cavity.
example: Its position helps maintain a temperature suitable for sperm production.
whatItDoes: Its position helps maintain a temperature suitable for sperm production.
feature: Its position helps maintain a temperature suitable for sperm production.
importantDistinction: Sperm form inside seminiferous tubules, not in the scrotal wall.
confusion: Sperm form inside seminiferous tubules, not in the scrotal wall.

meaning: A coiled tube inside a testis where sperm develop.
example: Developing reproductive cells move toward its lumen as they mature.
whatItDoes: Developing reproductive cells move toward its lumen as they mature.
feature: Developing reproductive cells move toward its lumen as they mature.
importantDistinction: Sperm maturation continues later in the epididymis.
confusion: Sperm maturation continues later in the epididymis.

meaning: A coiled duct beside a testis where sperm mature and can be stored.
example: Sperm develop the capacity for movement there.
whatItDoes: Sperm develop the capacity for movement there.
feature: Sperm develop the capacity for movement there.
importantDistinction: It is not the original site of sperm production.
confusion: It is not the original site of sperm production.

meaning: The duct carrying sperm from the epididymis toward the ejaculatory duct.
example: Muscular contractions move sperm along it.
whatItDoes: Muscular contractions move sperm along it.
feature: Muscular contractions move sperm along it.
importantDistinction: It transports sperm; it does not produce testosterone.
confusion: It transports sperm; it does not produce testosterone.

meaning: A duct formed where the sperm pathway joins the duct of a seminal vesicle.
example: It carries material into the urethra through the prostate.
whatItDoes: It carries material into the urethra through the prostate.
feature: It carries material into the urethra through the prostate.
importantDistinction: Sperm do not pass through the urinary bladder on this route.
confusion: Sperm do not pass through the urinary bladder on this route.

meaning: A passage carrying urine out of the body and, in the male reproductive system, carrying semen during ejaculation.
example: Semen leaves through the urethra within the penis.
whatItDoes: Semen leaves through the urethra within the penis.
feature: Semen leaves through the urethra within the penis.
importantDistinction: Urine and semen are normally released at different times.
confusion: Urine and semen are normally released at different times.

meaning: An accessory gland contributing fructose-containing fluid to semen.
example: Its secretion provides an energy source for sperm.
whatItDoes: Its secretion provides an energy source for sperm.
feature: Its secretion provides an energy source for sperm.
importantDistinction: A seminal vesicle adds fluid; sperm are produced in seminiferous tubules.
confusion: A seminal vesicle adds fluid; sperm are produced in seminiferous tubules.

meaning: An accessory gland surrounding part of the urethra below the bladder.
example: It adds fluid that contributes to semen function.
whatItDoes: It adds fluid that contributes to semen function.
feature: It adds fluid that contributes to semen function.
importantDistinction: It is not a sperm-production site.
confusion: It is not a sperm-production site.

meaning: An accessory gland releasing lubricating mucus into the urethra.
example: Its secretion helps prepare and protect the passage.
whatItDoes: Its secretion helps prepare and protect the passage.
feature: Its secretion helps prepare and protect the passage.
importantDistinction: It is also called a Cowper’s gland, not a seminal vesicle.
confusion: It is also called a Cowper’s gland, not a seminal vesicle.

meaning: The mixture of sperm and accessory-gland secretions.
example: It provides a fluid medium for sperm transport.
whatItDoes: It provides a fluid medium for sperm transport.
feature: It provides a fluid medium for sperm transport.
importantDistinction: Semen and sperm are not interchangeable names.
confusion: Semen and sperm are not interchangeable names.

meaning: An external reproductive organ containing the urethra.
example: It provides a route for depositing semen in the female reproductive tract.
whatItDoes: It provides a route for depositing semen in the female reproductive tract.
feature: It provides a route for depositing semen in the female reproductive tract.
importantDistinction: It transports semen; it does not produce sperm.
confusion: It transports semen; it does not produce sperm.

meaning: The process of producing sperm in seminiferous tubules.
example: It includes reproductive-cell divisions and subsequent differentiation.
whatItDoes: It includes reproductive-cell divisions and subsequent differentiation.
feature: It includes reproductive-cell divisions and subsequent differentiation.
importantDistinction: Meiosis has two divisions; differentiation into sperm is not another reduction division.
confusion: Meiosis has two divisions; differentiation into sperm is not another reduction division.

meaning: A supporting cell within a seminiferous tubule.
example: It nourishes and supports developing sperm and responds to FSH.
whatItDoes: It nourishes and supports developing sperm and responds to FSH.
feature: It nourishes and supports developing sperm and responds to FSH.
importantDistinction: Sertoli cells support sperm; they do not become sperm.
confusion: Sertoli cells support sperm; they do not become sperm.

meaning: A cell between seminiferous tubules that releases testosterone.
example: LH stimulates these cells.
whatItDoes: LH stimulates these cells.
feature: LH stimulates these cells.
importantDistinction: These are also called Leydig cells; they are distinct from Sertoli cells.
confusion: These are also called Leydig cells; they are distinct from Sertoli cells.

meaning: A reproductive starting cell that divides by mitosis in the testis.
example: It helps maintain a supply of cells for sperm production.
whatItDoes: It helps maintain a supply of cells for sperm production.
feature: It helps maintain a supply of cells for sperm production.
importantDistinction: It is not yet a mature sperm.
confusion: It is not yet a mature sperm.

meaning: A reproductive cell that begins meiosis I after DNA replication.
example: It can produce two secondary spermatocytes.
whatItDoes: It can produce two secondary spermatocytes.
feature: It can produce two secondary spermatocytes.
importantDistinction: It precedes the first meiotic division.
confusion: It precedes the first meiotic division.

meaning: A cell produced by meiosis I during spermatogenesis.
example: It undergoes meiosis II to produce spermatids.
whatItDoes: It undergoes meiosis II to produce spermatids.
feature: It undergoes meiosis II to produce spermatids.
importantDistinction: It has one chromosome set but the chromosomes have not yet completed sister-chromatid separation.
confusion: It has one chromosome set but the chromosomes have not yet completed sister-chromatid separation.

meaning: A haploid cell produced by meiosis II during sperm formation.
example: It differentiates into a specialised sperm.
whatItDoes: It differentiates into a specialised sperm.
feature: It differentiates into a specialised sperm.
importantDistinction: It is not a Sertoli support cell.
confusion: It is not a Sertoli support cell.

meaning: An enzyme-containing cap on the sperm head.
example: Its enzymes help sperm pass through layers around the egg.
whatItDoes: Its enzymes help sperm pass through layers around the egg.
feature: Its enzymes help sperm pass through layers around the egg.
importantDistinction: ATP supply is associated with mitochondria, not the acrosome.
confusion: ATP supply is associated with mitochondria, not the acrosome.

meaning: The long tail-like structure that produces sperm movement.
example: Its movement requires energy from ATP.
whatItDoes: Its movement requires energy from ATP.
feature: Its movement requires energy from ATP.
importantDistinction: It is not the location of the sperm’s main nuclear chromosome set.
confusion: It is not the location of the sperm’s main nuclear chromosome set.

meaning: The inner space of a tube.
example: Developing sperm are released toward the lumen of a seminiferous tubule.
whatItDoes: Developing sperm are released toward the lumen of a seminiferous tubule.
feature: Developing sperm are released toward the lumen of a seminiferous tubule.
importantDistinction: The lumen is a space, not a cell type.
confusion: The lumen is a space, not a cell type.

meaning: A process in which a cell becomes specialised in structure and function.
example: A spermatid develops sperm structures.
whatItDoes: A spermatid develops sperm structures.
feature: A spermatid develops sperm structures.
importantDistinction: Differentiation is not necessarily another cell division.
confusion: Differentiation is not necessarily another cell division.

meaning: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone, released by the hypothalamus.
example: It stimulates the anterior pituitary to release FSH and LH.
whatItDoes: It stimulates the anterior pituitary to release FSH and LH.
feature: It stimulates the anterior pituitary to release FSH and LH.
importantDistinction: GnRH does not come from the ovary or testis.
confusion: GnRH does not come from the ovary or testis.

meaning: Follicle-stimulating hormone, released by the anterior pituitary.
example: It supports Sertoli-cell activity in males and follicular development in females.
whatItDoes: It supports Sertoli-cell activity in males and follicular development in females.
feature: It supports Sertoli-cell activity in males and follicular development in females.
importantDistinction: Its name does not mean it has a function only in females.
confusion: Its name does not mean it has a function only in females.

meaning: Luteinizing hormone, released by the anterior pituitary.
example: It stimulates interstitial cells in males and helps trigger ovulation in females.
whatItDoes: It stimulates interstitial cells in males and helps trigger ovulation in females.
feature: It stimulates interstitial cells in males and helps trigger ovulation in females.
importantDistinction: LH and FSH leave the same gland but have different direct targets.
confusion: LH and FSH leave the same gland but have different direct targets.

meaning: An androgen released mainly by interstitial cells of the testes in the male pathway.
example: It supports reproductive function and many secondary sex characteristics.
whatItDoes: It supports reproductive function and many secondary sex characteristics.
feature: It supports reproductive function and many secondary sex characteristics.
importantDistinction: A high outside androgen signal can suppress upstream stimulation rather than increase sperm production.
confusion: A high outside androgen signal can suppress upstream stimulation rather than increase sperm production.

meaning: A group of hormones associated with male reproductive development and function.
example: Testosterone is the main example considered here.
whatItDoes: Testosterone is the main example considered here.
feature: Testosterone is the main example considered here.
importantDistinction: Human growth hormone is not an androgen or a steroid hormone.
confusion: Human growth hormone is not an androgen or a steroid hormone.

meaning: A hormone that helps limit FSH release.
example: Sertoli cells release inhibin as part of sperm-production feedback.
whatItDoes: Sertoli cells release inhibin as part of sperm-production feedback.
feature: Sertoli cells release inhibin as part of sperm-production feedback.
importantDistinction: It is a feedback signal, not a sperm-producing cell.
confusion: It is a feedback signal, not a sperm-producing cell.

meaning: A female gonad containing oocytes and hormone-producing follicular tissues.
example: It releases an oocyte at ovulation.
whatItDoes: It releases an oocyte at ovulation.
feature: It releases an oocyte at ovulation.
importantDistinction: The ovary does not travel into the oviduct.
confusion: The ovary does not travel into the oviduct.

meaning: A tube leading from near an ovary toward the uterus; the usual site of fertilization.
example: Cilia and muscular activity help move material toward the uterus.
whatItDoes: Cilia and muscular activity help move material toward the uterus.
feature: Cilia and muscular activity help move material toward the uterus.
importantDistinction: Fertilization in an oviduct is different from implantation in the endometrium.
confusion: Fertilization in an oviduct is different from implantation in the endometrium.

meaning: Fringed structures near the ovarian end of an oviduct.
example: They help guide a released oocyte toward the tube opening.
whatItDoes: They help guide a released oocyte toward the tube opening.
feature: They help guide a released oocyte toward the tube opening.
importantDistinction: The oviduct is not a sealed tube attached directly to the ovary.
confusion: The oviduct is not a sealed tube attached directly to the ovary.

meaning: A muscular organ supporting development after implantation.
example: Its wall contracts during labour.
whatItDoes: Its wall contracts during labour.
feature: Its wall contracts during labour.
importantDistinction: The endometrium is its inner lining, not the entire uterus.
confusion: The endometrium is its inner lining, not the entire uterus.

meaning: The inner lining of the uterus.
example: It grows and changes under hormone control and supports implantation.
whatItDoes: It grows and changes under hormone control and supports implantation.
feature: It grows and changes under hormone control and supports implantation.
importantDistinction: Menstruation sheds part of the lining, not the complete muscular uterine wall.
confusion: Menstruation sheds part of the lining, not the complete muscular uterine wall.

meaning: The narrow lower region of the uterus opening into the vagina.
example: It is part of the route sperm pass on their way toward the uterus.
whatItDoes: It is part of the route sperm pass on their way toward the uterus.
feature: It is part of the route sperm pass on their way toward the uterus.
importantDistinction: It is not an ovary or the usual fertilization site.
confusion: It is not an ovary or the usual fertilization site.

meaning: The passage connecting the cervix with the outside.
example: It receives semen and provides a route for menstrual flow and vaginal birth.
whatItDoes: It receives semen and provides a route for menstrual flow and vaginal birth.
feature: It receives semen and provides a route for menstrual flow and vaginal birth.
importantDistinction: It is distinct from the urethra.
confusion: It is distinct from the urethra.

meaning: The process producing the female gamete.
example: Unequal division retains most cytoplasm in one large reproductive cell.
whatItDoes: Unequal division retains most cytoplasm in one large reproductive cell.
feature: Unequal division retains most cytoplasm in one large reproductive cell.
importantDistinction: It does not normally produce four equally sized functional eggs.
confusion: It does not normally produce four equally sized functional eggs.

meaning: A developing female reproductive cell.
example: A secondary oocyte is released at ovulation.
whatItDoes: A secondary oocyte is released at ovulation.
feature: A secondary oocyte is released at ovulation.
importantDistinction: An oocyte is a cell within a follicle, not the whole follicle.
confusion: An oocyte is a cell within a follicle, not the whole follicle.

meaning: An ovarian structure containing an oocyte and supporting cells.
example: Growing follicles release estrogen.
whatItDoes: Growing follicles release estrogen.
feature: Growing follicles release estrogen.
importantDistinction: A follicle includes support tissue; it is not just another name for an egg.
confusion: A follicle includes support tissue; it is not just another name for an egg.

meaning: A temporary endocrine structure formed from follicular tissue after ovulation.
example: It releases progesterone and some estrogen.
whatItDoes: It releases progesterone and some estrogen.
feature: It releases progesterone and some estrogen.
importantDistinction: It remains in the ovary while the released oocyte enters a different route.
confusion: It remains in the ovary while the released oocyte enters a different route.

meaning: A small cell receiving relatively little cytoplasm during oogenesis.
example: Unequal division leaves most cytoplasm in the large reproductive cell.
whatItDoes: Unequal division leaves most cytoplasm in the large reproductive cell.
feature: Unequal division leaves most cytoplasm in the large reproductive cell.
importantDistinction: Polar bodies are not four equally sized eggs.
confusion: Polar bodies are not four equally sized eggs.

meaning: Shedding of part of the endometrium after a fall in ovarian-hormone support.
example: The first day of flow is day 1 of the cycle.
whatItDoes: The first day of flow is day 1 of the cycle.
feature: The first day of flow is day 1 of the cycle.
importantDistinction: Menstrual flow overlaps the early follicular phase.
confusion: Menstrual flow overlaps the early follicular phase.

meaning: The ovarian phase before ovulation, during which follicles develop.
example: Estrogen from a growing follicle supports endometrial rebuilding.
whatItDoes: Estrogen from a growing follicle supports endometrial rebuilding.
feature: Estrogen from a growing follicle supports endometrial rebuilding.
importantDistinction: Menstrual flow occurs within its early part, not before all follicular activity begins.
confusion: Menstrual flow occurs within its early part, not before all follicular activity begins.

meaning: Release of a secondary oocyte from a mature ovarian follicle.
example: An LH surge helps trigger this event.
whatItDoes: An LH surge helps trigger this event.
feature: An LH surge helps trigger this event.
importantDistinction: It is different from fertilization and from menstruation.
confusion: It is different from fertilization and from menstruation.

meaning: The ovarian phase after ovulation, characterised by corpus-luteum activity.
example: Progesterone supports the endometrium during this phase.
whatItDoes: Progesterone supports the endometrium during this phase.
feature: Progesterone supports the endometrium during this phase.
importantDistinction: It begins after ovulation, not after the next menstrual flow.
confusion: It begins after ovulation, not after the next menstrual flow.

meaning: An ovarian hormone that supports endometrial growth and participates in feedback.
example: A developing follicle releases rising estrogen.
whatItDoes: A developing follicle releases rising estrogen.
feature: A developing follicle releases rising estrogen.
importantDistinction: Sustained high pre-ovulatory estrogen can promote positive feedback, unlike its usual inhibitory contribution.
confusion: Sustained high pre-ovulatory estrogen can promote positive feedback, unlike its usual inhibitory contribution.

meaning: A hormone that supports and maintains the endometrium after ovulation.
example: The corpus luteum is a major source during the luteal phase.
whatItDoes: The corpus luteum is a major source during the luteal phase.
feature: The corpus luteum is a major source during the luteal phase.
importantDistinction: Its broad rise usually follows ovulation rather than being the LH surge that triggers it.
confusion: Its broad rise usually follows ovulation rather than being the LH surge that triggers it.

meaning: A large, brief increase in LH release associated with ovulation.
example: It follows sustained high estrogen in the normal model.
whatItDoes: It follows sustained high estrogen in the normal model.
feature: It follows sustained high estrogen in the normal model.
importantDistinction: A progesterone rise after ovulation is a different pattern.
confusion: A progesterone rise after ovulation is a different pattern.

meaning: A response that tends to oppose the initial change.
example: Rising testosterone reduces upstream stimulation.
whatItDoes: Rising testosterone reduces upstream stimulation.
feature: Rising testosterone reduces upstream stimulation.
importantDistinction: Negative means opposing the change, not harmful.
confusion: Negative means opposing the change, not harmful.

meaning: A response that reinforces or amplifies a change.
example: Sustained high pre-ovulatory estrogen promotes the LH surge.
whatItDoes: Sustained high pre-ovulatory estrogen promotes the LH surge.
feature: Sustained high pre-ovulatory estrogen promotes the LH surge.
importantDistinction: Positive does not mean healthy or permanent.
confusion: Positive does not mean healthy or permanent.

meaning: The end of menstrual cycling associated with declining ovarian follicular activity.
example: Reduced ovarian feedback can be associated with higher FSH and LH.
whatItDoes: Reduced ovarian feedback can be associated with higher FSH and LH.
feature: Reduced ovarian feedback can be associated with higher FSH and LH.
importantDistinction: Pituitary stimulation and ovarian responsiveness can change in different directions.
confusion: Pituitary stimulation and ovarian responsiveness can change in different directions.

meaning: Human chorionic gonadotropin, released by developing trophoblast tissue in early pregnancy.
example: It supports the corpus luteum and therefore continued ovarian-hormone support.
whatItDoes: It supports the corpus luteum and therefore continued ovarian-hormone support.
feature: It supports the corpus luteum and therefore continued ovarian-hormone support.
importantDistinction: hCG is not the progesterone made by the corpus luteum.
confusion: hCG is not the progesterone made by the corpus luteum.

meaning: Conception control using hormones or hormone-like substances to alter reproductive processes.
example: Combined methods can inhibit the normal LH surge and ovulation through feedback.
whatItDoes: Combined methods can inhibit the normal LH surge and ovulation through feedback.
feature: Combined methods can inhibit the normal LH surge and ovulation through feedback.
importantDistinction: Preventing conception is not the same as preventing STI transmission.
confusion: Preventing conception is not the same as preventing STI transmission.

meaning: A sexually transmitted infection.
example: Different bacterial and viral pathogens can affect health and reproduction.
whatItDoes: Different bacterial and viral pathogens can affect health and reproduction.
feature: Different bacterial and viral pathogens can affect health and reproduction.
importantDistinction: No obvious symptoms does not establish that no infection is present.
confusion: No obvious symptoms does not establish that no infection is present.

meaning: An organism or infectious agent capable of causing disease.
example: Bacteria and viruses cause different STIs.
whatItDoes: Bacteria and viruses cause different STIs.
feature: Bacteria and viruses cause different STIs.
importantDistinction: A hormone is a chemical signal, not a pathogen.
confusion: A hormone is a chemical signal, not a pathogen.

meaning: Inflammation involving upper female reproductive structures, often associated with infection.
example: It can damage oviducts and lead to scarring.
whatItDoes: It can damage oviducts and lead to scarring.
feature: It can damage oviducts and lead to scarring.
importantDistinction: Normal ovarian hormones do not guarantee an undamaged transport pathway.
confusion: Normal ovarian hormones do not guarantee an undamaged transport pathway.

meaning: Difficulty establishing a pregnancy due to one or more reproductive factors.
example: A damaged reproductive transport pathway can reduce fertility.
whatItDoes: A damaged reproductive transport pathway can reduce fertility.
feature: A damaged reproductive transport pathway can reduce fertility.
importantDistinction: It does not automatically mean that all gamete or hormone production has stopped.
confusion: It does not automatically mean that all gamete or hormone production has stopped.

meaning: A pregnancy implanted outside the normal uterine site.
example: Damage to an oviduct can increase the risk of implantation there.
whatItDoes: Damage to an oviduct can increase the risk of implantation there.
feature: Damage to an oviduct can increase the risk of implantation there.
importantDistinction: Normal fertilization in an oviduct is not the same as abnormal implantation there.
confusion: Normal fertilization in an oviduct is not the same as abnormal implantation there.
